title: In 2 Kings 12 What Does Joashs Early Faithfulness Teach Us About The Influence Of Godly Mentors
paragraphs: Joash’s Early Faithfulness: The Power of Godly Mentors

The story of King Joash in 2 Kings 12 gives us a powerful example of how godly mentorship can shape a life, especially in the formative years of leadership and faith. Joash’s reign began under the guidance of Jehoiada the priest, and his early days are marked by obedience to the Lord, inspired and directed by this godly influence.
Joash’s Background and the Role of Jehoiada

Joash ascended to the throne of Judah at just seven years old, after a perilous time when his grandmother Athaliah sought to destroy the royal family. It was Jehoiada, the high priest, who protected Joash and ultimately restored him to the throne (2 Kings 11:2). The text underscores Jehoiada's central role in both his survival and spiritual development:
And Jehoash did that which was right in the eyes of Jehovah all his days wherein Jehoiada the priest instructed him. - 2 Kings 12:2 ASV

Here, Scripture makes a direct link between Joash’s faithfulness and the mentorship of Jehoiada. This highlights the profound impact that a godly mentor can have in nurturing faith, wisdom, and obedience in the next generation.
The Importance of Godly Influence

Throughout the Bible, the value of spiritual mentorship is repeatedly affirmed. God often uses mature believers to guide, instruct, and encourage those who are younger in the faith. Consider these passages:
Train up a child in the way he should go, and even when he is old he will not depart from it. - Proverbs 22:6 ASV
And the things which thou hast heard from me among many witnesses, the same commit thou to faithful men, who shall be able to teach others also. - 2 Timothy 2:2 ASV

Joash’s story affirms that faithful instruction and godly modeling can lead to a life of obedience and service to God. Jehoiada’s influence established a foundation for Joash’s early reign, leading to reforms like the restoration of the temple (2 Kings 12:4).
Lessons for Today
Joash’s early faithfulness teaches us several important lessons:
Mentorship Matters: Spiritual growth is nurtured through wise, godly influence. Every generation needs faithful mentors to guide them.
Faithfulness Is Often Supported by Community: Joash thrived spiritually while Jehoiada was alive. We are called to encourage and exhort one another in the faith (Hebrews 10:24).
Passing the Torch: Mature believers are responsible to invest in the next generation, modeling a life of faith and obedience (Titus 2:3-7).
A Cautionary Note

Tragically, Joash’s faithfulness faltered after Jehoiada’s death (2 Chronicles 24:17). This underscores the need for personal conviction and relationship with God, not merely reliance on the faith of mentors.
Work out your own salvation with fear and trembling; for it is God who worketh in you both to will and to work, for his good pleasure. - Philippians 2:12 ASV
Conclusion

Joash’s early reign stands as a testament to the transformative power of godly mentorship. As believers, we are called to both seek and provide spiritual guidance, building up one another in the faith and pointing all generations to Christ as Lord and Savior.
